items.excerpt: ## Army Publishes New Map Showing Lead Dust from Munitions Plant Detonation Could Spread to Missouri Nov 25, 2026 Iowa Governor Kim Reynolds has declared a disaster emergency in three counties, as the U.S. Army prepares to detonate nearly five tons of highly unstable lead-based explosives at an ammunition plant in southeastern Iowa today. Environmental groups are warning of an unfolding public health catastrophe, with a detonation scheduled for 9 a.m. Central Time that could spew toxic lead dust across communities, farmland and potentially into the Mississippi River. Officials have recommended that residents of Middletown, where the plant is located, and anyone within a five-mile cone southwest of the plant evacuate, while people living up to 20 miles away have been told to stay indoors with their windows closed. This is Sean Kaufman, a disaster preparedness official with the Department of Health and Human Services. > Sean Kaufman: “Individuals that are in that directly affected area — which, again, we will continuously get updates based on the weather — if they are women who are pregnant, children under the age of 6, or children in general, and individuals who may have chronic disease, you definitely want to be out of that area. I would evacuate that area.” The Army published an updated map estimating the lead plume could spread all the way to northern Missouri, more than 100 miles from ground zero. There is no safe level of exposure to lead, a neurotoxin that can cause permanent cognitive and behavioral harm. Ahead of today’s detonation, The New York Times published an investigation revealing the Army had initially hired a firm to turn the explosives into harmless waste, but then dropped the contract in favor of a so-called controlled blast. items.title: GDP (Second Estimate) and Corporate Profits, 3rd Quarter 2026 | U.S. Bureau of Economic Analysis (BEA)
items.excerpt: EST, Wednesday, November 25, 2026 # GDP (Second Estimate) and Corporate Profits, 3rd Quarter 2026 Real gross domestic product (GDP) increased at an annual rate of 4.3 percent in the third quarter of 2026 (July, August, and September), according to the second estimate released today by the U.S. Bureau of Economic Analysis (BEA). In the second quarter, real GDP increased 2.2 percent. The contributors to the increase in real GDP in the third quarter were increases in investment, consumer spending, and government spending that were partly offset by a decrease in exports. Imports, which are a subtraction in the calculation of GDP, increased. Real GDP was revised up 0.9 percentage point from the advance estimate, primarily reflecting upward revisions to investment and consumer spending. For more information, refer to the " Technical Notes" below. Compared to the second quarter, the acceleration in real GDP in the third quarter primarily reflected an acceleration in investment and an upturn in government spending that were partly offset by a downturn in exports. Imports increased more in the third quarter than in the second quarter. Real final sales to private domestic purchasers, the sum of consumer spending and gross private fixed investment, increased 5.8 percent in the third quarter, revised up 0.9 percentage point from the previous estimate. The price index for gross domestic purchases increased 2.7 percent in the third quarter, revised down 0.3 percentage point from the previous estimate. The personal consumption expenditures (PCE) price index increased 2.1 percent, and the PCE price index, excluding food and energy increased 2.5 percent, both the same as previously estimated. Real gross domestic income (GDI) increased 4.4 percent in the third quarter, compared with an increase of 2.3 percent (revised) in the second quarter. The average of real GDP and real GDI also increased 4.4 percent, compared with an increase of 2.2 percent (revised).

items.title: US economy roars ahead in third quarter, inflation remains high in October
items.excerpt: WASHINGTON, Nov 25 (Reuters) - The US economy grew much faster than initially estimated in ‌the third quarter, while inflation increased further ​in October, reinforcing expectations ​that the Federal Reserve will raise interest rates next month and again in early 2027. The sharp upward revision to gross domestic product last quarter, reported by the Commerce Department on ... It reflected upgrades to consumer spending and business investment, mostly related to artificial intelligence. Robust domestic demand is fueling inflation, with a measure of underlying price pressures in October posting its biggest year-over-year increase since late 2023. ‌The economy has powered ahead despite the ongoing US-Israeli war with Iran. ... Growth in consumer spending, which accounts for more than two-thirds of the economy, was revised up to a 4.2% rate. That was the strongest pace since the fourth quarter of 2024 and was an upgrade from the previously ​reported 3.8% pace. Spending is being driven mostly by higher-income households, whose wealth was boosted by the stock market before the ongoing AI-led selloff. Economists expect consumer spending to slow to a still-healthy pace in the fourth quarter, though declining gasoline prices should ease some of the financial pressure on middle- and lower-income households. Average retail gasoline prices have dropped below $4 a gallon for the first time since mid-July, data from the US Energy Information Administration showed. ... The Personal Consumption Expenditures Price Index increased 0.3% in October after gaining 0.5% in September, the BEA said. PCE inflation was lifted by higher prices for goods, including food and household furnishings, as well as services such as recreation, dining out and hotel stays. In the 12 months through October, PCE inflation increased 3.8% after advancing 3.6% in September. Excluding the volatile food and energy components, the PCE Price Index increased 0.3% for the third straight month. So-called core PCE inflation increased 3.3% on a year-over-year basis in October, the largest advance since November 2023, after climbing 3.1% in September. The ‌Fed tracks the PCE price measures for its 2% inflation target. Financial markets have priced in a quarter-percentage-point rate hike at the US central bank's December 8-9 meeting from the current 3.75%-4.00% range, and are expecting another increase in January, CME Group's FedWatch tool showed. Fed Governor Christopher Waller has signaled he could support a bigger half-percentage-point rate increase to quell inflation. Economists, however, said tightening financial ‌market conditions amid an equities selloff had reduced the need for such an aggressive move.

items.excerpt: ## Trump administration blocked from carrying out the presidents’s renewed effort to limit Birthright Citizenship The Trump administration has been blocked from carrying out its executive order that would deny birthright citizenship to certain children of foreign government and international organization employees, as well as children born through surrogacy to non-U.S. citizens. U.S. District Judge Christopher Cooper wrote that the Supreme Court just last year made a very clear ruling on this issue, and he is following in its footsteps with this order. “The President cannot carve out new exceptions to birthright citizenship for children born within the United States and subject to its laws,” Cooper writes. “The Court will therefore certify a class consisting of children who are or will be unlawfully denied citizenship under the Order. And it will preliminarily enjoin the Government from enforcing the Order against members of that class.” “The Citizenship Clause promises citizenship to practically all children born in the United States. Earlier this year, the Supreme Court kept that promise by striking down EO1. This Court does so again today by enjoining EO2’s application as to the certified class.” A separate federal judge made a similar ruling in a separate case earlier this year.

items.excerpt: ## Daily Music Headlines November 25, 2026 Wednesday, November 25, 2026 U2 has announced the North American leg of its Greatest Show On Earth World Tour for 2027, with stadium dates beginning August 13 in Miami and wrapping October 18 in Vancouver. The tour includes two nights at MetLife Stadium and two at SoFi Stadium. Stephen Wilson Jr. opens the early dates, with The War on Drugs joining for the fall shows. U2.com subscriber presale begins November 30, with general tickets on sale December 4 through Ticketmaster. U2 Announces 2027 North American Tour Noah Kahan is releasing Live from the Great Divide on December 11. The 16-track live album captures performances from different cities on his 2026 tour. The first preview, “Orbiter,” recorded at Citi Field in New York, is out now with a video. Noah Kahan Announces Live Album Peter Gabriel has shared “Yes, It Will Go,” the penultimate song from his new album i/o. The piano ballad explores impermanence and features his daughter Melanie singing at the end. The full album arrives November 27. Peter Gabriel Shares “Yes, It Will Go” Wilco has announced 17 US dates for its Wilcoworld Tour, running April 20 through May 15, 2027. The tour includes a five-night stand at The Fillmore in San Francisco. Tickets go on sale November 27. An expanded Mermaid Avenue: The Complete Sessions, recorded with Billy Bragg, arrives December 14. Wilco Announces 2027 Tour Slipknot and Dr. Martens have announced a footwear collaboration arriving Black Friday. The collection features four shoe styles, along with socks, a card holder and a backpack, inspired by the band's visual identity and early boiler suits.
